Join a passionate fundraising team and make your mark on a new program that will help provide sustainable support for children with cancer and their families.

As Australia’s only national charity focused on the psychosocial needs of children with cancer and their families, Redkite provides practical, financial and emotional support throughout the cancer experience. Its services include counselling, music therapy, financial assistance, education, information and support for families navigating childhood cancer.

Redkite has recently launched an outsourced face-to-face regular giving program, and it is already tracking ahead of its ambitious first-year growth targets. This is an exciting opportunity to join at the beginning of the journey, take ownership of the program’s day-to-day coordination and help shape how regular donors are welcomed, engaged and retained over the long term.

As Regular Giving Coordinator, you will coordinate the face-to-face acquisition program, working closely with specialist agency partners, internal fundraising and database colleagues, and outsourced supporter relations providers. You will monitor performance, maintain high standards of donor care and ensure data moves accurately between suppliers and Redkite’s CRM.

This is a varied, hands-on role where no two days will look exactly the same. You might be reviewing acquisition and attrition metrics, resolving a donor enquiry, reconciling agency invoices, improving an internal process, developing regular giving content or helping agency fundraisers understand Redkite’s purpose and impact.

In this key role, you will:
  • Coordinate the day-to-day delivery of the face-to-face regular giving acquisition program
  • Build effective relationships with external fundraising and supporter relations agencies
  • Review existing reports, identify performance trends and recommend improvements
  • Ensure donor information is accurately transferred between agency partners, supporter relations providers and Redkite’s CRM
  • Support contract compliance, quality assurance and high standards of fundraiser conduct
  • Coordinate invoice reconciliation, clawbacks, cancellations and other program administration
  • Respond to regular giving enquiries and ensure donors receive a timely, positive experience

You understand how face-to-face regular giving programs work and are confident interpreting the core metrics that indicate whether a program is performing successfully.

You may already be coordinating a regular giving program, or you could be working in supporter care, donor services, individual giving or fundraising operations and be ready to take greater ownership. You enjoy working with data, systems and processes, but you never lose sight of the supporter experience behind the numbers.

You do not need extensive experience managing external agencies, as you will be well supported in agency meetings. However, you will bring the confidence to build strong supplier relationships, ask the right questions and ensure agreed standards and contractual expectations are upheld.

Most importantly, you are proactive, adaptable and motivated by the opportunity to build something. You can see where a process, communication or donor journey could be stronger and are willing to take the initiative to improve it.

  • Confidence working with donor data, reports and fundraising systems

job.description:

Reporting to the Chief Governance Officer & Company Secretary, you will provide governance and secretariat support to the Board, Committees and senior leadership team across multiple jurisdictions.
This role would suit someone with a legal background with governance, company secretariat and Board support experience. This role focuses on ensuring compliance with statutory, regulatory and governance obligations while contributing to the continuous improvement of governance frameworks, processes and reporting.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Supporting the Chief Governance Officer to manage end-to-end Board and Committee meeting processes, including agendas, papers, minutes and action tracking
  • Reviewing, drafting and coordinating Board and Committee papers to ensure quality, compliance and consistency
  • Maintaining statutory registers, governance records and corporate documentation
  • Management of all lodgments with ASIC and ACNC in a timely manner
  • Supporting corporate and regulatory reporting requirements
  • Coordinating the planning and delivery of the Annual General Meeting and any Extraordinary General Meetings
  • Managing governance calendars and governance-related reporting activities
  • Monitoring implementation of Board and Committee decisions
  • Conducting governance and regulatory research and recommend best practice
  • Support governance, risk and compliance reporting activities including the Annual Report and governance disclosures
  • Act as a point of contact for Board Members, Executives and Committee members regarding governance processes and documentation
  • Drive process improvements and efficiency's in the governance and secretariat functions
There is genuine opportunity for development and to take on increasing responsibilities under the guidance of an experienced Chief Governance Officer.

About You
We are looking for a governance professional who is trusted, accountable and operates with absolute discretion.
You will bring:
  • A degree in Law, Business, Commerce, Corporate Governance, or a related discipline
  • A legal background, qualification or experience within a legal environment will be highly regarded
  • Governance Institute qualifications (or Applied Corporate Governance certification) completed or in progress
  • Experience supporting Boards, Board Committees and senior executives in a governance function
  • Strong knowledge of corporate governance principles and governance processes
  • Experience maintaining statutory registers and governance records
  • Experience drafting, preparing or coordinating Board papers, minutes, resolutions or governance reports
  • Highly organized, who thrives on exceptional attention to detail, precision and professionalism.
  • The ability to manage highly confidential and commercially sensitive information
  • Strong written communication skills and confidence working with senior stakeholders
  • A proactive approach and willingness to continuously improve governance processes
  • Experience with Diligent or similar board paper platform is advantageous.
Personality fit:
  • Trustworthy, open, and transparent
  • Self-starter who looks for opportunities to improve
  • Act with integrity and discretion at all times
  • Communicate openly, professionally and transparently
  • Ability to influence and build relationships at all levels
  • Comfortable working independently while contributing to a collaborative team

This is a newly created role with the opportunity to join a values-driven organisation with a strong reputation, clear purpose and collaborative culture.  Working closely with experienced governance professionals and as part of a culture that values integrity, innovation, and growth.
